question: How should the Appearance list grow when a shape wants two shadows, a border on the inside, or a glow?
context: Appearance holds three rows today, Fill, Outline and Shadow, one of each. The effects asked for next do not fit: an inner and an outer border, an inner and an outer shadow, a glow, a bevel. Each option below is drawn as the panel for the SAME rectangle, a red fill, a border sitting inside the edge, and two drop shadows, so the three can be compared on one shape. The strips are in the brief.

options.label: One list you add to
options.summary: Fill and Outline stay where they are. At the foot of Appearance there is a plus whose menu names what you can add: Shadow, Inner shadow, Glow, Bevel. Anything you added carries a cross to take it away and a grip to drag it up or down, and the row at the top is the one painted nearest you. A border gains a Position of Inside, Centre or Outside; a shadow gains a Kind of Drop or Inner. Settings stay on screen while an effect is on, exactly as they do today.
pros: Nothing about a plain rectangle changes: the panel you use every day is the one you have now
Two shadows, and the second one is just another row with its own colour and its own numbers
A glow or a bevel arrives as one more line in the plus menu and teaches you nothing new
Keeps the answer you gave yesterday, that a switched on effect shows its settings without being asked
cons: A shape with two shadows is a very long panel: twelve slider rows, and you scroll the dock to reach the second one
Two ways to make an effect go away, the tick and the cross, sitting on the same row
options.mitigation: Only things you added can be removed, so a plain shape has just the tick and the cross never appears until you have asked for a second of something. If the length turns out to bite, an effect can learn to fold later without anything else changing.

options.label: One list, and an effect you are not editing folds to a line
options.summary: The same list, the same plus, the same cross and drag. The difference is density: an effect you are not currently editing shows its settings as a short summary on its own row, Drop 4 pt for one shadow and 4 pt Inside for the border, and clicking the row opens it. One effect is open at a time.
pros: Two shadows cost two lines instead of twelve, so the whole appearance of a shape is readable at a glance
The summary tells you what an effect is set to without opening it
The panel stays about the height it is today no matter how many effects you pile on
cons: It brings back a fold, which you asked to remove on 2026-09-06
Changing one number on each of two shadows means two clicks you do not pay today
options.mitigation: Unlike the fold that was removed, this one shows the values on the closed row, so a folded effect still answers the question you would have opened it to ask.

options.label: A fixed row for every effect
options.summary: No plus, no cross, no dragging. Appearance holds a permanent row with a tick for every effect the app knows: Fill, Outline, Inner Border, Shadow, Inner Shadow, Outer Glow, Inner Glow, Bevel. You find an effect by reading the list. You can never have two of anything, so a shape that wants a tight contact shadow and a wide soft one cannot have both.
pros: Everything the app can do is visible without opening a menu
One gesture only, the tick, so nothing can be accidentally removed
This is roughly the Photoshop layer effects list, which many people already know
cons: The common want, two shadows, is impossible
The list is long and mostly switched off, so eight rows greet you on a shape using two of them
Every new effect makes the panel taller for everybody, including people who will never use it
options.mitigation: Switched off rows can be pushed to the bottom so the ones in use stay at the top, but the list is still eight rows long on a shape using two.
